extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants (PIs, postdocs preparing K/K99/R01/SBIR) and institutional grant administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Practical community Q&A guidance on NIH grant submission/resubmission, mechanisms (R01, R56, K99, SBIR), paylines, interactions with Program Officers (POs), study section assignment, JIT, and award processing/timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of R56 (Bridge) awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The ultimate goal of the award is to provide interim, one-year support for investigators to collect preliminary data in support of a resubmission or newly competing NIH R01 application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use R56 to obtain data and make progress to improve a future R01; do not rely on it as a final award. Accepting R56 is generally recommended rather than turning it down because future budget/priorities are uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of funded application to R56 and effect on resubmission status
rubrics_metrics.description: If an A0 (original submission) is funded as an R56, that A0/A1 relationship changes: the prior A1 is withdrawn and you submit a new A0 (not an A1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You cannot submit a new A1 referencing the prior review if the A0 was converted to R56; instead submit a new A0, reference accomplishments from the R56 period, and clarify scope to avoid overlap with the R56 NOA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not overlap next R01 with R56 NOA scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever you have in your NOA as the scope of work for the R56 shouldn’t appear in the next A0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify with your PO what is allowable to avoid overlap; justify additional work based on data obtained during R56 period; new A0 may request more years (e.g., 5 years) if justified and typical for the IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carryover rules between R56 and R01
rubrics_metrics.description: The R56 counts as other support if the R01 is fundable. You may carry over funds from the R56 to the R01 if the R01 is awarded as a resubmission; a new R01 application will not allow for carryover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan budgets and timelines accordingly; discuss specifics with PO/GMS during JIT if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmit vs new R01 after R56 per NIAID SOP
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving an R56-Bridge award, submit an improved R01 using data resulting from the R56 award. You must submit either a resubmission (by revising your R01) or a new R01 application. Do not submit a renewal R01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify whether a resubmission or new A0 is appropriate with your PO; institutional grants staff and applicants often misunderstand this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on using prior review/response-to-reviewer when A0 converted to R56
rubrics_metrics.description: If A0 was converted to R56, you lose the benefit of the response-to-reviewer sheet because the prior review is not relevant anymore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead, reference progress made with R56 funding and new data; reviewers will probably remember the science even if formal prior review can't be referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing advice after receiving R56 (don’t rush resubmission)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the PO gave you an R56, they likely think you need more data; submitting again within weeks of receiving an R56 suggests you didn’t need it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wait sufficiently to accomplish work funded by R56 before resubmitting; discuss timelines with PO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective pay / end-of-FY selective pay process
rubrics_metrics.description: There is nothing applicants can do to request select pay consideration; POs generally advocate for applications to get on the list for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists for select pay are often set earlier in the FY and ICs work down these lists as funds are available; don’t expect to be able to ask for selective pay yourself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting automated NIH emails and status messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Automated emails can be confusing and sometimes refer to previous versions of your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm with your PO if an automated notice seems inconsistent; calling/emailing PO is often needed for clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: GMS assignment is not a reliable signal of funding
rubrics_metrics.description: A Grants Management Specialist (GMS) being assigned is generally irrelevant as a signal of funding likelihood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on priority score, PO communication, and JIT requests rather than GMS assignment to infer funding chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiscal year assignment and chance of cross-FY funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are assigned to a fiscal year based on submission cycle, but a peer-reviewed, Council-approved application can be funded in any FY as long as it is active (not administratively withdrawn).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although technically possible, ICs rarely go back to fund older FY applications; plan resubmission if you need timely funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim paylines vs final paylines
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim paylines are lower and indicate what ICs will consider for funding until later in the FY; final paylines are retroactive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on interim paylines to make application decisions; discuss resubmission vs waiting with your PO if your score is near the payline.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to consult your Program Officer (PO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your PO is the best source for advice on resubmission strategy, allowable overlap, carryover, start-date delays, and funding likelihood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact PO for clarifications but be aware they may be busiest at fiscal year transitions; ask concise questions and follow up after key dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study section (SRG) assignment advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: You can request a preferred study section in the application, but the SRO/IRG Chief makes the assignment decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unhappy with assignment, copy both SROs and the IRG Chief with a clear rationale; PO has no formal role in assignment but can advise on fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who reviews resubmissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmitted applications likely will include at least some of the same reviewers, but it is not guaranteed; reviewer availability and SRG membership affect assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect some continuity but write your resubmission to address prior concerns thoroughly; discuss with PO if reviewer continuity is a concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling RPPR final reporting deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: If your institution fails to submit a final RPPR by the deadline, typically the award will not be affected immediately; the institute (not the PI) is responsible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow up with sponsored programs office and PO if delays persist; a few days late usually won't be fatal, but correct promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/phase II timing, funding windows, and CR impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR Phase II awards can be paid in the intended FY or in later months depending on appropriations/CRs; FY assignments and start dates may be delayed by continuing resolutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect potential delays to start dates during budget uncertainty; talk with PO and budget office about implications for project timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-cost extension and carryover questions for SBIR
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for carryover and no-cost extension vary by mechanism (e.g., SBIR); applicants should talk with PO about what is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PO may not show sympathy for competing obligations; be proactive in discussing pandemic-related or legitimate delays with PO and institutional offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: K99 eligibility clock and counting postdoctoral years
rubrics_metrics.description: K99 PA states: 'Applicants must have no more than 4 years of postdoctoral research experience at the time of the initial (new) or the subsequent resubmission application.' NIH policy indicates eligibility clock may start at PhD conferment for some applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm with PO/IC how they calculate the 4-year limit (submission date vs due date vs PhD conferment). Use available extensions (e.g., COVID-related) and communicate extenuating circumstances to the IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIGMS K99 program preferences (timing/length)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIGMS expects one year of a postdoc for K99 and generally disfavors funding postdocs longer than ~5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider timing of application relative to career stage and publications; consult PO for NIGMS-specific expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use PAS-specific set-aside funds appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: A PAS (Program Announcement with Set-Aside) usually has set-aside money for the Program and intends to fund a limited number of meritorious applications; evaluation is relative to other PAS applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scores relative to regular R01 percentiles may be less informative; check PAS wording about intended number of awards and consult PO.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESI and special percentile adjustments / award durations
rubrics_metrics.description: Some ICs (e.g., NHLBI) provide extra percentile points for ESIs on certain renewals or second Type 1 R01s; established investigators may be limited to 4-year R01 awards while ESIs or clinical trials may get 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify IC-specific policies for ESI boosts and typical award durations; discuss with PO when planning project length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to summary statements and PO advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving a summary statement, you can ask your PO about next steps and whether they will advocate for your application (including select pay).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POs may have attended the meeting and can provide insight beyond the written summary; advocacy can influence select pay consideration but is limited by IC budget/priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to resubmit vs wait (insurance submission)
rubrics_metrics.description: If your score is at or just above the prior payline and you have important timing constraints (e.g., eligibility clocks), you should consider submitting again as insurance rather than waiting for budget clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss resubmission strategy with PO; frequently recommended to submit an 'insurance' application if timing matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attaching biohazard/SOP documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If an IC is considering funding the application, the PO or Grants Management Specialist will request SOPs (eg, for biohazards) during JIT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare SOPs in advance and be ready to submit them when asked in JIT requests to avoid delays in award processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical communication etiquette with SRO/IRG/PO
rubrics_metrics.description: When contesting or requesting study section assignment, copy both SROs and the IRG Chief and present clear, professional rationale; be mindful not to 'annoy' SROs with unnecessary messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concise, well-reasoned emails to the correct officials (SROs and IRG Chief) are effective; IRG Chiefs can and do change assignments when justified.
